_comment: False positives (ts-rust flags an error real tsc under --strict+extras does not) are the more damaging failure mode -- they reject valid code. Gaps (tsc catches something ts-rust doesn't yet) are expected and not gated here; the checker is still a work in progress. Current known false positive: tests/fixtures/builtin-generics/promise_member_access_correctly_reports_missing_property.ts -- Promise<T> is a deliberately opaque, unmodeled type (no .then()/await support yet), so accessing .then on it is honestly reported as missing even though real tsc's actual Promise has it; that fixture's own comment documents this as an intentional, expected divergence, the same category as array_indexing_dynamic_key_includes_undefined.ts. This replaces an earlier note about guard_clause_in_block_does_not_leak.ts, which has since been fixed and renamed to guard_clause_in_block_does_survive.ts. If a NEW false positive shows up alongside this one, maxFalsePositive should rise to 2 with its own explanation added here, not silently absorb it under this one's allowance -- and if/when Promise gets real .then() modeling, drop this back to 0.
